result.topic_en: Derivation, for a surface or moving frame with direction cosines and parameters t, u, of expressions for derivatives a', b', c', a'', b'', c'' and an integrability condition $\partial a'/\partial u = \partial a''/\partial t$ leading to an equation for $\partial^2 \log m/\partial t^2 + \partial^2 \log m/\partial u^2$.
result.transcription:
$a' = \frac{am' - \alpha m''}{m} - A(aA'+bB'+cC')$
$b' = \frac{bm' - \beta m''}{m} - B(aA'+bB'+cC')$
$c' = \frac{cm' - \gamma m''}{m} - C(aA'+bB'+cC')$
$a'' = \frac{\alpha m' + am''}{m} + cB' - bC'$
$b'' = \frac{\beta m' + bm''}{m} + aC' - cA'$
$c'' = \frac{\gamma m' + cm''}{m} + bA' - aB'$
$a''A' + b''B' + c''C' = -\frac{\theta m'}{m} + \frac{m''}{m}(aA'+bB'+cC')$
$\alpha'A'' + b'B'' + c'C'' = -\frac{\theta m'}{m} + \frac{m''}{m}(\alpha A'' + \beta B'' + \gamma C'')$
$Bc'' - Cb'' = \frac{-am' + \alpha m''}{m}$
$Ca'' - Ac'' = \frac{-bm' + \beta m''}{m}$
$Ab'' - Ba'' = \frac{-cm' + \gamma m''}{m}$
$a' + \alpha'' = -A\, mmn$
$b' + \beta'' = -B\, mmn$
$c' + \gamma'' = -C\, mmn$
$[-na-]\, na' = (\frac{m'}{m} - AA')(A' + CB'' - BC'') - AB'(B' + AC'' - CA'') - AC''(C' + BA'' - AB'') - \frac{m''}{m}(A'' + BC' - CB')$
$[-n-]\, nb' = (\frac{m'}{m} - BB')(B' + AC'' - CA'') - BC'(C' + BA'' - AB'') - BA''(A' + CB'' - BC'') - \frac{m''}{m}(B'' + CA' - AC')$
$nc' = (\frac{m'}{m} - CC')(C' + BA'' - AB'') - CA'(A' + CB'' - BC'') - CB''(B' + AC'' - CA'') - \frac{m''}{m}(C'' + AB' - BA')$
$na'' = \frac{m'}{m}(A'' + BC' - CB') + \frac{m''}{m}(A' + CB'' - BC'') - A(A'A'' + B'B'' + C'C'')$
$nb'' = \frac{m'}{m}(B'' + CA' - AC') + \frac{m''}{m}(B' + AC'' - CA'') - B(A'A'' + B'B'' + C'C'')$
$nc'' = \frac{m'}{m}(C'' + AB' - BA') + \frac{m''}{m}(C' + BA'' - AC'') - C(A'A'' + B'B'' + C'C'')$
Die Formel $\frac{\partial a'}{\partial u} = \frac{\partial a''}{\partial t}$ gibt uns folgende Gleichung
$\alpha\left(\frac{\partial\partial \log m}{\partial t^2} + \frac{\partial\partial \log m}{\partial u^2}\right) + \frac{m''}{m}\left(a' + \frac{\partial\partial x}{\partial u^2}\right) + A''(aA' + bB' + cC') + A(a''A' + b''B' + c''C') + c'B' - b'C'$
$+ A\left(a\frac{\partial\partial A}{\partial t\partial u} + b\frac{\partial\partial B}{\partial t\partial u} + c\frac{\partial\partial C}{\partial t\partial u}\right) + c\frac{\partial\partial B}{\partial t^2} - b\frac{\partial\partial C}{\partial t^2} = 0$
Und eben so zwei andere ganz ähnliche; multiplicirt man sie respective mit $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ und addirt, so erhält man
$mm\left(\frac{\partial\partial \log m}{\partial t^2} + \frac{\partial\partial \log m}{\partial u^2}\right) + (aA' + bB' + cC')(\alpha A'' + \beta B'' + \gamma C'') + \Sigma\, \alpha(c'B' - b'C') + \Sigma\, \alpha\left(c\frac{\partial\partial B}{\partial t^2} - b\frac{\partial\partial C}{\partial t^2}\right)$
$= 0$
Die beiden letzten Theile sind $= [-\Sigma-] \frac{\partial\, \Sigma\, \alpha(cB' - bC')}{\partial t} - \Sigma\, a''(cB' - bC')$
Nun aber ist
$cB' - bC' = A\theta$
$aC' - cA' = B\theta$
$bA' - aB' = C\theta$
wo $\theta = -\frac{A'A'' + B'B'' + C'C''}{n}$
also $\Sigma\, \alpha(cB' - bC') = 0$ folglich auch dessen Differential $= 0$
Ferner $\Sigma\, a''(cB' - bC') = \theta(Aa'' + Bb'' + Cc'') = -\theta(aA'' + bB'' + cC'')$
$= +\theta\theta$
